append.text: **Ps 25:4 *Non sedi cum concílio vanitátis* (συνεδρίου) → *Não me sentei no conselho da vaidade*** — decided locally as D34 directs; draft 1 had *com o conselho*, and the blind reader heard advice (a recommendation dictated by vanity), so the preposition changed, not the word: one sits *in* a council. The gate Latinist (minor) wants *com* back for *cum*'s company; refused, draft 1's words stay the option.

**Ps 25:5 *Odívi ecclésiam malignántium* → *Odeio a assembleia dos malvados*; 25:12 *in ecclésiis benedícam te, Dómine* → *nas assembleias vos bendirei, Senhor*** (D34 applied; the Lavabo's last line). No reader remarked.

**Ps 25:5 *Odívi* → *Odeio*** — the Latinist's MAJOR on draft 1's *Odiei*, taken: *odi* is a perfect with present sense (24:19 *odérunt* → *me odeiam*, the same ruling). **118:104 *odiei* should be re-read by it.**

**Ps 25:10 *déxtera eórum repléta est munéribus* → *a direita deles está cheia de dádivas*** — the stylist asked for *presentes* (*dádivas* 'solemn'); refused for this row, *presentes* kept as the option; the blind reader heard gifts first, bribes by inference, as at 14:4b.

**Ps 25:3 *complácui in veritáte tua* → *achei prazer na vossa verdade*** — another build (*complacére in*, take pleasure in; εὐηρέστησα ἐν); draft 1's *me comprazi* was 'livresco' to the stylist and unknown to the blind reader. Candidate for the other *complacére in* places (grep before copying).

**Ps 25:4 *cum iníqua geréntibus non introíbo* → *com os que fazem coisas iníquas não entrarei*** — *gérere*, a third build: kept apart from *ágere* (→ agir) and *operári* (→ praticar). The stylist wanted *os que praticam iniquidades* and the verb moved first; refused (operári's verb; the verb last is the Latin's cadence, as 25:5 *não me sentarei*); his line is an option.
**Ps 25:1, 25:11 *in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum* → *andei na minha inocência*** — applied; the blind reader heard the conduct rightly.
**Ps 25:8 *diléxi decórem domus tuæ* → *amei o esplendor da vossa casa*** — applied; the stylist's best line (the Dedication versicle, C8.txt).
**Ps 25:2 *ure renes meos et cor meum* → *queimai os meus rins e o meu coração*** — applied; the blind reader again heard the organ and the inmost self.

**Ps 25:9 *Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam* → *Deus, não façais perecer com os ímpios a minha alma*** — the vocative moved first at the stylist's request; the Passiontide versicle stands alone.
**Ps 25:2 *Proba me, Dómine, et tenta me* → *Provai-me, Senhor, e experimentai-me*** — see the new row *tentáre*.

terms: | tentáre | experimentar where God tests the psalmist (*Provai-me, Senhor, e experimentai-me*); *tentar* where men tempt God | open | Ps 25:2 *tenta me* — draft 1's *tentai-me* was heard by the blind reader first as "lead me into sin"; *experimentar* is free and kept apart from *provar* (probáre) in the same colon, safe at the *vós* imperative (past *experimentei*). Where men tempt God (77:18, 77:41, 77:56, 94:8 *tentavérunt me … probavérunt*, 105:14; grep) *tentar* is heard rightly and can stay; 34:16 *tentavérunt me* (men trying the psalmist) decides there; the noun *tentátio* 17:30, 94:8. |

| *in concílio / ecclésia sedére* | *sentar-se no …* (*Não me sentei no conselho da vaidade*) | open | Ps 25:4; the preposition *em*, not *com*, so the body is heard and not advice (the blind reader). 1:1 *in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit* is another build. |

| lavare manus (*Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas*) | lavar as mãos entre os inocentes (*Lavarei as minhas mãos entre os inocentes*) | open | Ps 25:6 (the Lavabo); 72:13 *et lavi inter innocéntes manus meas* should copy it (*e lavei as minhas mãos entre os inocentes*). The blind reader heard the idiom of disclaiming responsibility — the Latin's own image, from which the idiom comes; kept. |
formulas: | *Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas: * et circúmdabo altáre tuum, Dómine* … *in ecclésiis benedícam te, Dómine* (25:6–12, the Lavabo of the Mass, identical in DO Ordo.txt / Ordo67.txt; Quad5-3's Communion is another wording, *circuíbo*) | *Lavarei as minhas mãos entre os inocentes: * e cercarei o vosso altar, Senhor:* … *nas assembleias vos bendirei, Senhor.* | open — Ps 25; the whole stretch must read alone from 25:6 (it does: 25:6 opens a sentence) |

| *Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam. R. Et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam* (25:9; the Passiontide versicle, Minor Special.txt, Psalmi matutinum.txt) | *Deus, não façais perecer com os ímpios a minha alma. R. Nem com os homens de sangue a minha vida.* | open — Ps 25 |
| *Júdica me, Dómine, quóniam ego in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum* (25:1; Introit of Quad2-1) | *Julgai-me, Senhor, porque eu andei na minha inocência* | open — Ps 25 |
